evidence: HColorSet.parseColor handles transparent/background/automatic before parseSimpleColor, but gradient endpoints use parseSimpleColor only.

findings.summary: Rust does not preserve HColorSet's whole-color none resolution for transparent/background named notes.
evidence: component_solid_transparent_background_valid.java.svg renders TransparentSolid and BackgroundSolid note paths with fill="none"; the Rust SVG renders the same note paths with fill="#FEFFDD".
deployment_solid_transparent_background_valid.java.svg renders TransparentSolid and BackgroundSolid note paths with fill="none"; the Rust SVG renders the same note paths with fill="#FFFFFF".
The Rust parser stores the raw token, but the downstream renderers do not carry Java's HColors.none result.

accepted_residue: Java PlantUML 1.2026.3beta6 accepts #automatic as a whole named-note color but crashes during SVG rendering with HColorAutomagic; this was preserved but not used as the primary rejection because the Java reference itself does not produce a normal diagram.

The Java error pages for invalid probes report assumed diagram type component even for deployment-like sources; this appears to be PlantUML's assumption text in the error renderer, not a Rust finding.
conclusion: The claimed ColorParser.exp1/HColorSet equivalence is disproved. The implementation conflates whole-color parseColor specials with parseSimpleColor gradient endpoints, and it does not propagate HColors.none semantics for transparent/background through the observable Rust output. Verdict: REJECT.
